role: Reviewed intent. Human-edited. Lists every snow texture to generate.

conventions.evidence: Verified against MSR788_Rifle: the muzzle attachment offset Y=0.4968 equals the mesh maximum Y=0.4966, the scope attachment sits at Z=+0.0491 above the bore at Z=+0.0308, and a textured side render is upright only with +Z up and V used directly.
conventions.warning: Up sign is now recovered from geometry by the grip-side test in generate_snow_textures.ps1 and checked against the spec on every run: the grip or stock is the largest mass off the bore line and it points down. It splits cleanly on all nineteen meshes, with handguns at upSign -1 and long guns at +1. Two earlier heuristics failed exactly on handguns. The contact sheet remains the second check, and it now renders each weapon the way it is held.
conventions.stageProgression: noiseBase and edgeSoftness are IDENTICAL across the stages of one weapon, on purpose. The mask keeps one noise field and only lowers the threshold, so each stage's snow is a superset of the previous stage's. Re-rolling the field per stage would make snow appear in different places between stages, which reads in game as snow teleporting when a threshold is crossed. Only targetUpCoverage, flankCoverage and flankMaxAlpha vary.
conventions.wiring: Model blocks and EW_Profiles.lua are generated by tools/generate_mod_wiring.js from this spec plus the vanilla ModelScript attachments. vanillaModel names the ModelScript to copy attachments from; modelName is the EW model that the profile selects for that stage.
conventions.saturation: targetUpCoverage never reaches 1.0. Once the up-facing region of a UV island is fully covered, the visible snow edge is no longer the mask boundary but the edge of the geometry, and on a cylinder like a barrel or handguard that edge is a straight line by definition. Keeping a margin of holes at every stage is what makes the transition read as organic. Stage 4 is 'heavily snowed with gaps', not 'buried'.
conventions.flank: flankMaxAlpha stays well below opaque at every stage. A flank is a near-vertical surface, so snow there is thin by definition; letting it reach 0.90 made large flat flanks like a shotgun stock side fill with solid white, which reads as a painted rectangle rather than snow. The flank pass is a dusting and its alpha ceiling has to say so.
conventions.wetness: Wet entries carry mode='wet' and a NEGATIVE stage, matching the signed state axis in EW_Config: positive stages are snow, negative are wet, 0 is vanilla. They carry the SAME geometry keys as snow -- targetUpCoverage, flankCoverage, flankMaxAlpha, noiseBase, edgeSoftness -- copied from one of the weapon's own snow stages (1, 2 and 4 for the three levels), and add only wetMaxAlpha. Water builds from the top down and creeps onto the flanks exactly the way snow does; only the compositing differs, darkening where snow whitens. An earlier version gave water a pool field of its own with every surface but the undersides eligible, and in game it read as scattered staining rather than as weather.
